Can the same edge be used multiple times in a single path, and are there any restrictions on revisiting vertices?
When multiple shortest palindrome paths exist with the same length, does the output need to reflect any tie‑breaking rule or is the length alone sufficient?
Are self‑loops (edges from a vertex to itself) allowed, and if present, do they count as a single‑character palindrome of length 1?
Is the length of a path defined as the number of edges traversed, the number of characters in the concatenated label string, or something else?
Must the palindrome condition be satisfied by the entire concatenated string, or is it sufficient for some prefix or suffix to be a palindrome?
Are the characters '-' guaranteed to appear only where no edge exists, and can they ever be considered as a valid label character?

inline_prompts: We have a directed graph with N vertices, numbered 1, 2, \ldots, N. Information about the edges is given by N^2 characters C_{1, 1}, C_{1, 2}, \ldots, C_{1, N}, C_{2, 1}, \ldots, C_{N, N}. Here, each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -. If C_{i, j} is a lowercase English letter, then there is exactly one directed edge from vertex i to vertex j labeled C_{i, j}. For each integer pair (i, j) with 1 \leq i, j \leq N, answer the following question: - Among all (not necessarily simple) paths from vertex i to vertex j whose concatenation of labels on the edges forms a palindrome, what is the length of the shortest such path?
